title: Thermal activation of photon catalysis in difference-intensity Mach-Zehnder interferometry with squeezed thermal light
abstract: Realistic non-Gaussian operations, which can be implemented by mixing a nonclassical Gaussian state with a Fock state at a beam splitter and then heralding on a photon-number-resolving detector, are known to improve phase estimation in a Mach-Zehnder interferometer. The existing studies have considered the single-mode squeezed vacuum for difference-intensity and parity detection, and the two-mode squeezed thermal state for parity detection alone as the initial Gaussian resources. However, a real squeezer in the lab actually produces single-mode squeezed thermal light, which has not been studied in a coherent-plus-resource interferometer. We take up this case and using the phase space Wigner picture, we obtain the heralded state produced by photon subtraction, addition and catalysis on a single-mode squeezed thermal resource, and evaluate the corresponding phase sensitivities. Single-photon catalysis, which is useless on squeezed vacuum, becomes a useful operation for any thermal occupation above $\nth\simeq0.2$, and since it heralds with a probability near one-half, it turns out to be the best success-weighted operation over the whole thermal range. In the vacuum limit our results reproduce the known hierarchy, where two-photon catalysis is the best operation. The quantum Fisher information computations confirms that thermal noise enhances the phase information encoded in the catalyzed state, demonstrating that difference-intensity detection closely approaches the ultimate precision bound across most operational regimes, and, together with a loss analysis, verifies the robustness of the effect.
summary: This work analyzes phase estimation in an MZI using squeezed thermal light, focusing on the role of photon catalysis. It finds that unlike vacuum resources, thermal noise activates single-photon catalysis as the best measurement strategy for moderate thermal occupations. The results confirm that difference-intensity detection remains highly robust and close to the ultimate precision limit.
main_problem: The paper investigates how non-Gaussian operations, specifically photon catalysis, can enhance phase estimation in a Mach-Zehnder Interferometer (MZI) when using realistic single-mode squeezed thermal light as the quantum resource.
main_result: Single-photon catalysis emerges as the optimal success-weighted operation for thermal occupations above a threshold ($n_{th} \gtrsim 0.2$), demonstrating that thermal noise enhances the encoded phase information and maintains robustness against losses.
method: The analysis employs the phase space Wigner picture to calculate the Quantum Fisher Information (QFI) and phase sensitivity ($\Delta\phi$) for the difference-intensity observable.
model_or_system: The system models an MZI where the resource state is a single-mode squeezed thermal state. Non-Gaussian states are generated by mixing this resource with an ancillary Fock state and heralding on the output.
key_observables: Phase sensitivity ($\Delta\phi$), Quantum Fisher Information (QFI), and the difference-intensity observable ($\hat{O}$).
important_parameters: Squeezing parameter ($r$), thermal occupation ($n_{th}$), and beam splitter transmissivity ($	au$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the realistic preparation of the non-Gaussian state via mixing with a Fock state and subsequent heralding.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the MZI setup for difference-intensity detection and the schematic for preparing the realistic non-Gaussian state using the resource and an ancilla.
paper_structure: The paper builds from the general problem of phase estimation using non-Gaussian operations, details the specific model involving squeezed thermal light, derives the heralded Wigner function, and finally computes the phase sensitivity using QFI.
why_interesting: It provides a detailed theoretical analysis of how realistic noise sources (thermal photons) interact with advanced quantum resources (squeezing) to optimize quantum metrology protocols, showing a non-trivial crossover in optimal measurement strategies.

Two-photon subtraction gives the largest raw advantage over the whole thermal range, and single- photon catalysis goes from a useless operation at nth = 0 to a strongly useful one. FIG. 4. Optimized difference-intensity phase uncertainty ∆ϕ against the squeezing r at nth = 0.5, q0 = 10, ϕ = π/2. The bare squeezed thermal resource is the solid black curve. Single-photon catalysis improves the sensitivity over the whole displayed squeezing window.

FIG. 5. Phase quantum Fisher information Fϕ of the heralded single-mode resource as a function of thermal occupation nth at r = 0.3, evaluated using Eq. (20). While two-photon catal- ysis and the bare squeezed thermal resource carry more phase information but decrease with thermal noise, single-photon catalysis is ineffective on vacuum and actively switches on with thermal occupation.
